findings.title: The real TLS, custom CA and SNI tests are replaced by mocks or marked ignored, so CI no longer checks the rustls client.
findings.body:
Before this change, `sends_requests_with_custom_ca_and_sni` started a local HTTPS server with a generated CA. That test checked that the built-in `reqwest::Client` factory trusts the custom CA, sends the SNI name and rewrites the Host header over a real handshake. `accepts_inline_and_file_ca` checked that a valid PEM CA is accepted, and the rotation tests used real CAs.

Now the TLS test uses `MockTokenProxyClient`, which never calls the `reqwest_rustls` implementation. The CA-acceptance and end-to-end tests are `#[ignore]`d and need a live AKS pod, and the rotation tests use mock factories that accept any bytes. With `reqwest_rustls` enabled, CI no longer tests that `TokenProxyClient for reqwest::Client` (`tls_backend_rustls`, `add_root_certificate`, `resolve_to_addrs`) loads a valid CA or completes a handshake. This change edits exactly that code's feature gating. A regression there, such as a missing `reqwest/rustls` feature at runtime or a broken CA parse, would pass every non-ignored test.

The issue only asked to move the feature flags. Fix: keep at least one non-ignored positive test of the real client, such as the old in-process TLS server test or a checked-in test CA for `accepts_inline_and_file_ca`, alongside the new mocks.

findings.title: Rewrites the live-test provisioning and skip logic, which the feature-flag issue did not ask for.
findings.body:
Issue #5550 only asks to move `reqwest/rustls` from the `reqwest` feature to `reqwest_rustls` and adjust the `cfg` gating. This PR also does unrelated work:
- It rewrites the post-provisioning script: a new required `IDENTITY_DEPLOY_RESOURCES` Bicep output, readiness and endpoint polling, and `az account set` outside CI.
- It removes the `CI_HAS_DEPLOYED_RESOURCES` early return from the ACI and workload identity live tests.
- It turns the IMDS live test from a skip into a hard failure and marks it ignored.

The removed skips change behaviour. In a live-mode run where `deployResources` is false (the Bicep default), `aci_user_assigned_live` and `workload_identity_credential::tests::live` now panic on `expect("IDENTITY_..._IP")` instead of skipping. I could not see whether the CI live pipeline always deploys resources. Fix: split the test-infrastructure changes into their own PR, or confirm the live pipeline always sets `deployResources`.

held.title: `azure_core_test` now turns off `azure_identity` default features, so it loses its HTTP transport and the built-in token proxy client.
held.body: Before this change, `azure_core_test` got `azure_core/default` and `reqwest_rustls` through `azure_identity`'s default features. `azure_core_test` itself depends on `azure_core` with `default-features = false`. When it is built alone (for example `cargo test -p azure_core_test`), or by a consumer that doesn't otherwise enable `azure_core` defaults, it may now have no Reqwest transport and no TLS backend. Live credentials created through `Recording::credential()` would then fail at runtime. The issue doesn't ask for any change to this shared test crate. I could not see whether every consumer re-enables these features through workspace feature unification. Fix: revert this line, or explicitly enable the features `azure_core_test` needs, such as `features = ["reqwest_rustls"]`.
